A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sloth work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite reformatting, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original performance-prediction errors, latent-skill analyses, downstream-task predictions and test-time scaling evaluations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical analyses and adds MAPE evaluation results in Appendix H.1.

M1.justification: Section 4.6 and Appendix B add a post-fitting procedure that selects parameter and token allocations to maximize a learned skill under a fixed compute budget and data-support bounds. The underlying Sloth architecture, training objective and fitting procedure are retained.

E1.justification: The model roster, 12 leaderboard benchmarks, HumanEval, EQ-Bench, AgentBench and MATH test-time evaluation are retained. The new allocation tables derive configurations from the existing model rather than evaluate additional datasets or environments.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the FLOPs variants, PCA+FLOPs, Size and Tokens, and the observational-scaling comparator in Appendix L. The added MAPE figure uses the existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix H.1 adds evaluation using MAPE alongside MAE. Existing cross-validation rules, one- and two-model training conditions, model configurations and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds a metric-sensitivity check using MAPE, a parameter-count analysis and a compute-budget allocation analysis. Existing latent-dimension, shared-intercept, link-function and downstream case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports run counts, seeds, error bars or significance tests. The new checklist explains the existing omission of error bars but introduces no uncertainty estimates or changed statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical figure content is unchanged. New Figure 10 reports MAPE results, including average errors of 11.3 for Sloth d=4 on leaderboard v1 and 18.0 for d=3 on v2. Tables 1–2 add model-derived optimal allocations.

T1.justification: Section 4.6 and Appendix B derive a bounded quadratic optimization from the existing skill law under 6st=c. Appendix F adds a parameter-count argument. The identifiability theorem and assumptions are retained, with an intermediate algebraic step expanded.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add deriving compute-optimal scaling rules for skills as a contribution. The principal claims about cross-family prediction, interpretable skills, downstream prediction and test-time scaling are retained.

C2.justification: v5 adds the interpretation that optimal allocations are family-independent under its model and bounds allocations to limit unsupported extrapolation. The checklist adds a non-iid-data rationale for omitting error bars. Existing predictive and identifiability limitations are mostly relocated and clarified.

D1.justification: v5 newly states that fitting and prediction take seconds on a commercial laptop and describes quantile-based bounds for allocation analysis, without specifying the quantiles. Existing Huber/Adam, network and rotation details are retained despite relocation; the code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4.6 newly positions compute-optimal skill scaling against the validation-loss allocation analyses of Kaplan and Hoffmann. Those works were already cited; the bibliography and the main positioning against Owen and Ruan are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most prose remains intact. Model fitting moves from Appendix C to Section 3.2, detailed rotation instructions move to Appendix A.1, and limitations move into the conclusion. v5 also adds subsections, acknowledgements and a checklist, and updates affiliations.

P2.justification: The main text switches from two columns to a single-column NeurIPS layout, with extensive figure resizing and repositioning. v5 adds MAPE Figure 10 and allocation Tables 1–2, and corrects three correlation-plot captions. Existing plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: v5 makes resource allocation concrete through a bounded optimization and allocation tables, adds a useful MAPE sensitivity check, and makes fitting details and limitations easier to locate. These are limited gains over the retained evidence. Appendix F introduces the arithmetic error 12(f+5)=50+12f rather than 60+12f, but correcting it does not overturn the stated parameter-efficiency comparison for f>=4.
